findings.summary:
Candidate fc93a30 (attempt 4 plus the test-only attempt 5) resolves the feature-r2 deadline major and the evidence parts of the reliability major. The historical quarantine cause is still unknown and travels as an explicit carried limitation.

Deadline truth is fixed at the source. request-queue.readinessTime() reads the immutable primary ready_at from the bridge command/event inside the existing transaction. It does no content decode, calls no public producer and takes no serializer. It also requires the adopted namespace, private_bridge_complete() and ready_at == recorded_at, and it quarantines on any inconsistency rather than falling back to the clock. As a result, `late` is ready_at > due whenever readiness exists, and the old rule applies otherwise. PrepareLateUpdate's breach_observed inherits that value, so readiness on or before the due time stays on time across later reads, support updates and withdrawal, and genuinely late readiness stays late. Paired on-time, exactly-due and late tests and the Root probe cover the queue projection, parent home, founder overdue filter and immutable effects.

The review-journal and review-service changes are passive diagnostics only. I verified that canonicalization of the fail() arguments cannot throw for values that passed the existing guards, so sticky `broken`, the marker/MAC checks and the generic errors are unchanged. The React waits are now deadline-based, and the two test-only fixture fixes keep the exactly-due instant and the marker-validation boundary.

Final-source evidence:
- One checks() sequence with three consecutive full suites (each 319 tests: 316 pass, 0 fail, 3 platform skips).
- Build, protected 04-C (27 diagnostics, unchanged) and all five probes, including the paired deadline probe.
- Seven native cases bound to the exact blobs.
- Archived logs show no failed final-source run.

Zero plays and introduction-only remain. Full 05-A/B/G and 08-A/B stay OPEN and 07-A/B stay DONE.

findings.title: Carried: historical review-release quarantine cause remains UNKNOWN
findings.problem: The first full run on 60a4613 hit recovery_quarantined in review.command(ReleaseTestSnapshot), and its cause is still unattributed. The recovery delivered the contracted capability instead: sanitized boundary and opaque-hash capture in review-journal and review-service, with sink exceptions contained, no private fields, and tests for privacy and non-interference. There was no recurrence across the later full runs: bd8c563 (whose failures were only the two fixture defects), three consecutive fc93a30 suites, the probes and two diagnostic rounds. Non-recurrence is not causal proof. I am downgrading my r2 reliability major because the remaining failure mode is fail-closed (sticky denial, no data exposure or false success), its origin is the accepted upstream review path rather than bridge writes, and the required capture and three-pass evidence now exist. It is not waived and must stay visible. Also note that the observer set is process-wide and reviewIntegrityDiagnostic is an exported emitter that any importer could call. It confers no authority, but its records are not authenticated forensics, as the guide already says.
findings.fix_check: The partial receipt and REPORT keep the quarantine listed as UNKNOWN and not waived. Any recurrence in later work must be captured with the boundary and hash records and attributed before related producer changes are accepted.

findings.problem: The native limitations disclose that the first fixture's JSON was overwritten, so its IDs and timestamps come from the tool transcript. They also disclose that one exploratory positive held-response wait was fenced by an intervening automatic poll. The direct-read sequence is proven by the controlled React test (three passes) rather than by native evidence. Both are disclosed and do not undermine the seven cases, but they weaken the native receipt's independent reproducibility.
